title: LLM runner: embed a lightweight Go LLM client for the ladder's budgeted agent stage — non-streaming completions, per-call budgets (tokens+wall-clock), config-driven model + fallback chain, context-compaction hook
description: the maintainer directive 09-16: lightweight LLM framework, avoid wastefulness — the daemon runs under stress, so STREAMING IS A NON-GOAL (one buffered request/response per stage; a hung stream is the failure mode we refuse). Plain net/http against OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoints (NO heavy SDKs — this is the lightweight framework). Config: [llm] blocks with base_url/api_key-ref/model/max_tokens/timeout per role, plus fallback_chain = ordered endpoint list; a stage tries candidates in order on transport/5xx/429 errors, records which candidate served in the ledger. Context compaction: before each stage, if the assembled context exceeds a configured budget, run a map-style compaction pass (summarize-per-chunk via the same client, single-shot, capped) and record compaction in/out token counts in the ladder record — interesting-but-accountable, never silent truncation. Skill-library support: the ladder's skills stage reads skills from a local dir in Claude-skill format (SKILL.md + frontmatter) so a REMOTE agent can author/build skills and the daemon picks them up (pull-down = git or dir mount; matches SPEC-11 skill loop + the 'remote agent will build the skill' requirement). Budgets: hard caps enforced pre-request (max_tokens) and mid-call (wall-clock timeout), over-budget = stage fails budgeted, never runaway. SPEC-05 §agent and SPEC-11 need §-amendments (letter-suffix) for the [llm] config schema + compaction contract; selfcheck must PASS.
acceptance_criteria: internal/llm client: buffered completions only (no SSE/stream), configurable endpoint/model/key-ref, timeout enforced
fallback chain: config-ordered candidates, failover on 429/5xx/transport, serving candidate recorded in the ledger stage record
context compaction hook: over-budget context triggers capped single-shot compaction, token counts recorded, never silent truncation
skills: ladder reads a local skill-library dir (SKILL.md format) and can execute a skill step against the runner
SPEC-05/11 letter-suffix amendments + selfcheck PASS
tests: client contract test (httptest server), fallback test, budget-exceeded test

title: Host-load-sensitive Go gates: `make check` / `go test ./...` are RED at fleet load_avg >= 45 (TestAmortizedThroughput 29049 vs load-derived floor 37453; TestDeriveNeverBlocks; TestCollectorLongLineIsTruncated) — make the host-measured floors load-aware at high load, or fence them out of `make check` with an explicit skip verdict
description: Found during TRBL-001 verification (2026-09-17, host load_avg 45). The v0.1 wave already made the ledger throughput floors and seven host-measured wall-clock budgets load-aware, but the load-aware form still fails ABOVE ~load 45: `go test ./... -count=1 -short` reds out in internal/research (TestDeriveNeverBlocks), internal/sentinel (TestCollectorLongLineIsTruncated) and internal/ledger (TestAmortizedThroughput, 29049 rec/s against a load-derived floor of 37453 and a spec floor of 100000 / measured 515k). `make check` therefore exits 2 and cannot be used as a pre-push gate on a busy fleet host. Verified pre-existing: the same tests fail identically on a pristine `git archive HEAD` (a6881de) control tree, so this is NOT TRBL-001 collateral. Two honest exits: (a) derive the floor from measured host capacity per run (the existing load-aware form only scales to a point) and/or make the assertion a ratio against a no-scrub baseline, or (b) split `make check` so host-measured perf gates are a separate target with an explicit SKIPPED verdict under high load, so the specs/tools gates stay a reliable gate.
acceptance_criteria: the failing tests are either green or explicitly SKIP (never silently weakened) at load_avg >= 45
any skip is recorded with the observed load_avg and the measured value, in the test output

title: [P0] The shipped examples/config.toml cannot boot: verify.zone_windows is an inline TOML table, the parser accepts only the SPEC-12 §167 k=v string - boot refuses with TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001 before any listener opens
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17: `cp examples/config.toml ~/dogfood-trouble/config.toml` (the path docs/cmd.md + deploy/README.md both point a new operator at) then `bin/troubled --config config.toml` refuses to boot: err="TROUBLE-LIFECYCLE-001: key \"verify.zone_windows\": bad zone_windows pair \"{\"" (exit 13, no listener, daemon never serves). examples/config.toml:65 uses TOML inline-table syntax `zone_windows = { loopback = "10m", ... }`; internal/lifecycle/config.go:433 applyToMapStringDuration accepts map[string]any OR the documented space-separated string, and the TOML decoder hands it a scalar `{`-leading string that fails the pair split. SPEC-12:167 pins the accepted form: `verify.zone_windows` default `loopback=10m lan=15m tailnet=20m public=30m`. So the example file contradicts the spec it ships with, and the FIRST key a fresh user meets is a boot refusal. review_notes: Evidence: 401 TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002 vs 200 after the absolute token_file; token hash match; verbatim transcript in docs/dogfood/2026-09-17-integration.md.
title: [P0] Stock config yields a dashboard that can never authenticate: the default dashboard.token_file is the literal path ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json and `~` is never expanded, so a MISSING file reads as a valid EMPTY token set - every Bearer token 401s TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002 with no log line and no health signal
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, reproduced twice on the control host. With examples/config.toml (which sets no dashboard.token_file) the daemon boots and serves :7644, but `trouble dashboard token create` mints a tdt_ token that the SAME daemon rejects: GET /incidents -> 401 {"error":{"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002","message":"authentication failed"}} - on a daemon started AFTER the token existed. The token hash in ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json matches sha256(plaintext) exactly (verified), so mint and store agree; the daemon simply never loaded the file. Mechanism: dashboard.DefaultConfig() TokenFile = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json" (internal/dashboard/config.go:58, a literal tilde); internal/app/dashdeps.go:43 only overrides it when the lifecycle key is non-empty; nothing expands ~ inside the dashboard package, os.Stat fails, and tokens.go readFileIntoSet documents "a missing file yields a valid empty set" - so it fails closed, silently, forever. Proof of the mechanism: with the identical build, config and token, adding `token_file = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json"` to [dashboard] and restarting flips GET /incidents from 401 to 200 rendering "Incidents - trouble" (15 KB). Blast radius: the dashboard (SPEC-10) is unreachable and the ONLY credential the product can mint is inert, on the documented config path; tests/e2e/cli_smoke.sh passes only because it hands the daemon an absolute token_file. Fix direction: expand ~ (or resolve the path through the same resolver the CLI uses) in DefaultConfig/dashboardConfig, and log a WARN whenever the token store loads as missing/empty so the failure is not silent.
acceptance_criteria: a stock examples/config.toml boot accepts a CLI-minted token on /incidents (200)
the resolved token_file path is proven identical between `trouble dashboard token create` and the daemon (asserted by a test)
an empty/missing token store logs a WARN at boot (fail-closed stays, silence does not)
cli_smoke.sh gains a case that exercises the DEFAULT token_file path, not only an explicit one

title: [P0] Three of five subsystems are silently not built on a stock config (sentinel: no projects configured, issues: driver github needs owner+repo, skills: source_path/source_url) - the ingest on-ramp never opens and /health.json reports only a generic degraded
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17. Booting examples/config.toml writes a `subsystem_not_built` lifecycle record per refused subsystem on EVERY boot (12 records across 4 boots): sentinel: "no sentinel projects configured" (internal/app/subsystems.go:386 buildSentinel returns nil for len(projects)==0); issues: "TROUBLE-ISSUES-003: config_invalid: driver github needs owner and repo (SPEC-09 3.9.1)"; skills: "TROUBLE-SKILLS-001: config_invalid: exactly one of source_path or source_url must be set". Consequences observed: (a) nothing ever listens on ingest.bind 127.0.0.1:7643 - POST /api/1/event/ is connection-refused, so the README's headline on-ramp ("POST /api/{id}/event/, one curl from any runtime") is impossible; (b) /health.json returns status="degraded" with detail={"sensor_degraded":"inotify"} - it names a sensor, never the three absent subsystems, and has no `subsystems` key at all; (c) the dashboard surfaces nothing either, so the documented "absent means no such record" rule only works if an operator knows to grep the ledger; (d) boot exits 0 and the daemon serves, so nothing looks wrong. There is also no documented (or implemented) way to declare a project: no CLI verb, no config key reachable through `trouble config explain` - sentinel's project set is only ever passed in-process (SubsystemOptions.SentinelProjects), so an operator cannot enable the ingest plane at all. Fix direction: populate SentinelProjects from config ([[projects]] with id/public_key/secret), surface a `subsystems` block (name, built, refusal code) in /health.json + the dashboard, and make the README's on-ramp example reachable from the shipped example config. LATER SAME RUN (sharper evidence): with a rules.d installed (examples/rules/10-defaults.toml copied to <state_root>/../config/rules.d/) the daemon reports /health.json status="ok" with detail=null and all six sensors degraded=false - while the same boot's ledger still carries the three subsystem_not_built records (sentinel: no sentinel projects configured; issues: TROUBLE-ISSUES-003; skills: TROUBLE-SKILLS-001). So the health surface does not merely under-describe a degraded boot: on a clean-shaped config it issues a GREEN light for an instance whose ingest plane, issue desk and skill loop are absent. That is the project's own named anti-pattern ("never observe itself into a green lie") reproduced on the health surface, and it is why this row is P0.
acceptance_criteria: a stock boot cannot report status="ok" while any subsystem was refused (regression test over a boot with no projects configured)
a documented config surface declares projects (id + DSN public key) and the ingest listener actually binds

review_notes: Evidence: ledger aggregation by sig/inKey/kind with timestamps, quoted in docs/dogfood/diagnostics.md.
title: [P1] Idle-host amplification: 778 records / 74 incidents in 6 minutes from an idle host with 21 distinct sigs - the same sig AND same inKey re-opens a new incident 3-4x (69-142s apart) and one psi sig produced 137 event records
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, measured on a throwaway state root against the live control host (idle, loadavg ~7 but no app activity). Over 6 minutes the daemon wrote 778 ledger records: 684 event, 74 incident, 16 lifecycle, 4 config; ledger grew to 843 KB; /health.json reported events_per_min 204, groups_open 96, incidents_open 74. Only 21 distinct sigs and 21 distinct inKeys exist, yet 74 incident records - i.e. 3-4 incidents per identity: e.g. sig dbus:sha256v1:c158b3e1eac71459 with inKey ink_... at 16:02:10, 16:03:19, 16:05:41 (69s and 142s apart). SPEC/README pin the dedup+merge upsert keyed by sig+inKey with a fold inside the dedup window (AC-22) - same key, same window, new incident. Event level: one psi sig (psi:sha256v1:f8525bc3eea25477) accounts for 137 of 684 event records in 6 min, i.e. the same recurring observation is persisted every sensor cycle. The dbus storm breaker did fire ("rule:dbus_unit_failed: 21 incidents inside 5m0s"), so the breaker works while the fold does not. Projection: ~180k records/day and ~200 MB/day of ledger from ONE idle host, before any real incident; the ledger is append-only, git-distributed and auto-filed, so this growth is permanent. Ask: verify the dedup fold (window values, key derivation, upsert path) and add a per-rule event fold/suppression so a repeating condition is one record with a count, not N records.
acceptance_criteria: a repeated detection with identical sig+inKey inside the dedup window yields ONE incident (test over the real ingest/sensor path)
a repeating rule does not persist one event record per cycle (fold or counter, with the disposition visible)

title: [P2] Dashboard polish from real use: footer renders an empty version (`trouble v ()`), the budget panel's first server render after boot is blank/zero (fills ~2s later), and the auth-failure throttle 429s a VALID token after prior failures from the same IP
description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, all three observed live on a throwaway state root (autonomy=shadow). (1) Every page footer renders `trouble v () - read-mostly dashboard (SPEC-10)` while /health.json reports version c363daf / git_sha c363daf and the budget partial renders "c363daf c363daf" - the footer's version value is empty at render time, so the operator's most visible build stamp is missing while the build is correctly stamped elsewhere. (2) The /incidents page fetched immediately after boot server-renders the budget panel with empty values (`binary`/`rss`/`ledger`/`events` blank, groups open 0, incidents open 0) in the SAME response whose header says "open incidents (74)"; 9 s later /partials/budget carries the real numbers (13.7 MB, 96 groups, 74 incidents). First paint therefore contradicts itself until the first poll lands - and the numbers ARE available (runtime_watermarks in the same /health.json). (3) The auth-failure throttle keys on the client IP, not the credential: after 8-10 failed attempts from one IP (a mistyped/rotated token, or the pre-fix 400s), requests carrying a VALID token get 429 {"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-012","message":"rate limited","detail":"auth_failure_throttle"} with Retry-After: 1 for the whole 60s window. Fix direction: render the version into the footer from the same accessor the health surface uses; seed the first budget render from the same watermark source; and either key the failure throttle on (IP + credential class) or surface a distinct banner so a legitimate operator understands they are throttled, not rejected. (4) heartbeat.json is written with ledger_last_seq=0 and ledger_last_ts="" on every heartbeat - observed across three instances including one whose ledger held 188 records - so the liveness surface a human or an external monitor reads reports a permanently zero sequence while the ledger is advancing (check-stall uses the ledger directly and is unaffected; the field is simply always empty). Fold the same fix as (1): source these values from the accessors that already answer correctly elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: footer shows the version/git_sha the health surface reports
a page fetched within the first seconds after boot renders budget values consistent with its own header counts

This is an infra row, not a trouble-code row: the follow-up is to fix/diagnose bunker spawn against agent-host-3 (or re-run the leg) so the next tick can start from zero state. Two trouble-side installability observations collected from the repo in the absence of the bunker leg, both already covered on the board: (a) the repo has NO git remote (`git remote -v` empty), so no fresh machine can `git clone` it and any fresh install must start from an archive - relevant to TRBL-002's release matrix; (b) the documented install path is `make bin` + `trouble install [--scope user|system]` (deploy/README.md) and `make bin` appears in docs/cmd.md but NOT in README.md - folded into TRBL-008.
acceptance_criteria: a subsequent dogfood tick on trouble completes the bunker install leg (clone-or-archive + documented install + documented smoke) OR the spawn failure is root-caused and fixed
the install leg's measured seconds and smoke verdict land in .coding-hermes/dogfood-log.md
if the failure is reproducible, an infra row lands on the bunker/hosts owner with the verbatim spawn error and the reachability evidence

title: [P1] QA discovery audits non-repo stub workdirs: every '*qa' scheduler row is picked with its stand-in workdir, so a full bunker battery runs against a directory with no source (real project stays 'never-qa')
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes:
qa_discover.py excludes '-pm'/' -sync'/dogfood/sync names but NOT '-qa' role rows (12 enabled in scheduler.db). Those rows' workdirs are stand-in stubs: /stand-in/pm/ holds only .coding-hermes/board (a symlink to the real board) and no source, and is not a git repo. Live repro: `python3 /scripts/qa_discover.py 2` -> picks -qa (repo=/stand-in/pm/) + hermes-canopy-qa (repo=.../pm/hermes-canopy), both reason=never-qa. Pipeline checkpoint evidence (run /tmp/dagger-role-qa-1730745-*): project=terminal-jail-qa, repo=/stand-in/pm/terminal-jail, run_battery raw='ERROR: /stand-in/pm/terminal-jail is not a git repo' yet the same node returned launched:true. Consequences: (a) 2 discovery slots/tick burn a bunker slot for nothing, (b) the interpreter turns its own 'not a git repo' into a P1 finding about the harness and files it on the REAL project board (live example: QA-TERMINAL-JAIL-QA-1 on ~/terminal-jail), (c) the DuckBrain record lands under '-qa' so qa_discover never marks the real project QA'd -> the same stub gets re-picked. Fix: exclude '*-qa' + 'qa-audit' in qa_discover.py; map '

-qa' picks to base project p and its real workdir; drop launched:true when the launch failed.

title: [P1] Launch retry ladder leaks live bunker agents and truncates the evidence file: the first attempt's agent is still running (orphan) and `: > $EVIDENCE` wiped its cells
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Tick dogfood-trouble-qa (started 17:01:46 local, targeted ~/trouble). Timeline from the run DB + evidence files: (1) agent cefd6920 created 2026-09-17T15:02:30-07:00 on agent-host-2, registered+running, referenced by NO evidence file on the box (grep over /tmp/*.jsonl|*.meta|*.log = 0 hits) -> orphan from the first attempt; (2) second spawn ed361cdd 15:06:20-07:00 owns the successful launch (`launch` cell OK at 22:10:15Z, script_bytes=19056); (3) TWO concurrent `tar --warning=no-file-changed -C ~/trouble | ssh` pipelines were observed at 15:08 local -> at least two launch attempts in flight, both writing the SAME evidence path; (4) both attempts truncate the evidence file at entry (`: > "$EVIDENCE"` in launch()), which is why the first attempt left nothing behind. Net: one live agent leaked (holds a slot until its 4h TTL), one attempt's evidence lost. Fix: destroy the agent before retrying, make evidence paths per-attempt (or append-only), and make spawn_agent clean up an agent it cannot use.

title: [P1] QA sync ships the whole workdir including gitignored build artifacts: ~/trouble = 141 MB of which 111 MB is .worktrees/ -> phase A took 8.5 min against a documented 60-120s budget
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Measured on the control host: `du -sh --exclude=.git ~/trouble` = 141M, of which `.worktrees/` = 111M (8 stale worker worktrees, each carrying its own `.git` file), `dagger.db` = 68K, `bin/` (stamped binaries) and `.gitreins/` are shipped too. src: bunker-qa.sh sync_repo() tars with a hardcoded exclude list (.git, node_modules, target, .next, .pnpm-store, .turbo, .cache, dist, build, coverage) and never consults .gitignore. Observed on the agent: ~/qa-trouble = 110 MB with .worktrees at 96 MB, then remote `git init && git add -A && git commit` over that payload inside a 1800s ssh budget. Phase A measured: tick start 17:01:46 -> `launch` cell 17:10:15 = 8.5 min (documented expectation 60-120s) with two syncs in flight, on a ~600 KB/s pipe. Secondary consequence: the untracked, gitignored dagger.db is exactly what the chaos-corruption cell picks as its 'state file' (QA-TROUBLE-3), so the battery corrupts a build artifact instead of real state. Fix: build the payload from `git archive`/`git ls-files` (tracked files only), honour .gitignore, and add a size guard with a visible FAIL cell.

title: [P1] file_findings reports FILED=1 / write_failed:false while the board commit failed: `fatal: pathspec '.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl' is beyond a symbolic link` — the row lands uncommitted
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Checkpoint output of the file_findings node (run /tmp/dagger-role-qa-1730745-1789670827473332851, project terminal-jail-qa): APPENDED=1 PRIOR=134 TOTAL=135 / FILED=1 / 'fatal: pathspec '.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl' is beyond a symbolic link' with write_failed:false and verdict FINDINGS. Verified on disk: the row exists (~/terminal-jail/.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl contains QA-TERMINAL-JAIL-QA-1, 135 rows) and `git -C ~/terminal-jail status --porcelain` shows ` M .coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl` = UNCOMMITTED. Cause: the stand-in workdir path is a directory symlink chain (.coding-hermes/board -> real repo board), and git refuses to add a path that traverses a symlink. Since the target is the '-qa' stand-in for every stub pick, this silently applies to all of them. Fix: resolve the board path with readlink -f before add/commit, and treat a git failure as filed=false (the node must not report success when the commit failed).

title: [P2] Bunker substrate degraded: agent-host-3 wedged (8/8 users, 0 registered, every spawn deadline_exceeded) and agent-2/agent-4 also refused spawns today — install verification (QA battery + dogfood install leg) could not run
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: agent-host-3 (ssh bunker3, bunkerd active): `bunker spawn --server agent-host-3 --ttl 2h` -> 'deadline_exceeded: context deadline exceeded' after ~300s, and the box's journal shows NO spawn attempt in that window; on disk 8 bunker users with max_agents: 8 (from /etc/bunkerd/config.yaml), all their bunker-docker-* units inactive, one broken user (bunker-b97e8e8c: home dir with no passwd entry), and the registry reports 0 agents -> the box can never accept a spawn again without manual cleanup. agent-host-2: 32 users on disk vs 6 registered agents, 5 running dockerds on 6 CPUs; my install-leg spawn there also returned deadline_exceeded. agent-host-4 (1 agent, <project>-lab): same deadline_exceeded, and no new agent appeared server-side afterwards. Doctrine drift to fix alongside: bunker-qa.sh still says agent-3 'was REMOVED from ~/.bunker/config.yaml' while config.yaml registers it (connected_at 2026-09-10), and the dogfood skill still names agent-host-3 as THE install box. This repeats TRBL-011 (SKIPPED-install-bunker, 2026-09-17) and QA-TERMINAL-JAIL-1 (port-pool exhaustion). Fix: reaper for agent users with no registry entry, a `bunker reap`/`destroy --orphans` command, and one authoritative list of live servers consumed by both the skill and bunker-qa.sh.

title: [P2] No git remote: a fresh user cannot obtain this repo at all — no clone URL anywhere, README documents build+test only, and the Go toolchain version is never stated
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — install path could not be walked as documented
review_notes: `git remote -v` in ~/trouble = empty, so there is no url to `git clone` and no `go install github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/trouble/cmd/trouble@latest` target although go.mod declares that module path (the QA battery only ever ships the tree by tar-over-ssh from the control host). README's install surface is the 'Build and test' block (go build ./... / go test ./internal/...); it never says how to get the source, which Go version is required (go.mod: go 1.26 — QA's own bootstrap used go 1.26.5), or that `make bin` is the stamped build. Consequence: the README's implied promise ('self-hosted incident brain') cannot be fulfilled by anyone outside this host, and every QA/install run depends on a control-host tar stream instead of a documented fetch. Fix direction: publish the repo (module-path rename commit is already the plan) with a clone URL + a Quickstart (fetch, toolchain version, make bin, make smoke, first boot), and make `make smoke` the documented smoke check.

title: [P1] The QA lane grades and closes a run CLEAN one minute into a 7-15 minute battery: single collect attempt, filed:0, real cells never pulled, agent left to TTL
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 (target row trouble-qa) — QA lane field test
review_notes: Observed end to end on the targeted tick: `launch` cell written 22:10:15Z (battery started detached, toolchain-bootstrap OK / fresh-install in progress on the agent at 22:10:45Z), then `parse_cells` ran its ONE PHASE-B collect attempt at ~22:11Z, got RUNNING (early-exit, no destroy), and the pipeline went straight to `interpret` (22:11:13) and `file_findings` (22:11:19) -> verdict CLEAN, findings [], filed 0, summary 'phase-B collect has not reported results, so no findings are derivable'. The battery was ~1 minute into a 7-15 minute run; its later cells (ci-pass, chaos-*) were never collected, no ledger row records them, and the agent is left to its 4h TTL. This is the premature-completion pattern the QA lane exists to catch, implemented in the lane itself: the verdict is honest about having no evidence, but the RUN still terminates as CLEAN, so a failing CI/chaos cell produces no row, no gap, no retry. Design quotes (hermes-dagger examples/coding-hermes/qa.ts ~L150-190): 'PHASE A: LAUNCH, never wait ... Phase B (collect) runs at the top of parse_cells and pulls the cells once it has finished; if nothing collects it, the agent's TTL (default 4h) reclaims it.' Fix direction: poll collect to completion (bounded, e.g. until ~20 min) before interpreting, or emit an explicit UNVERIFIED/deferred row + a scheduled second pass so the finished cells reach the board; never let a still-running battery end as CLEAN.

title: [P1] Clean-machine native suite is RED: TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange fails on a fresh bunker box but passes on the control host (mtime-fingerprint assertion is filesystem/host fragile)
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 — cell recovered by collecting the battery the QA lane closed CLEAN before it finished (QA-LANE-6)
review_notes: Battery on agent-host-2 (agent ed361cdd, tree synced from HEAD 28c3c01, go 1.26.5 bootstrapped): ci-pass FAIL 'native rc=1: FAIL github.com/totalwindupflightsystems/trouble/internal/sensors 74.846s ...' with the failing test verbatim: '--- FAIL: TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange (0.00s) | reload_test.go:310: the mtime fingerprint did not change after an edit'. Control host, same commit: `go test ./internal/sensors/ -run TestRuleDirMTimesDetectsChange -count=1` -> ok 0.006s at load_avg 3.08, i.e. PASS. So this is clean-machine/environment-specific, not a deterministic break: the assertion compares mtimes after an edit, which depends on the filesystem's mtime granularity and on the tar-synced tree's timestamps on the agent (the battery ships the tree via tar + `git init && add -A && commit`, so file times are rewritten). Same env-fragility family as QA-TROUBLE-1 (RSS budget) and QA-TROUBLE-2 (scrub wall-clock budget). Fix direction: make the fingerprint check granularity-independent (compare content hashes or force mtime with explicit values after a sleep >granularity), and note it in the reload contract; then re-run the clean-machine cell to confirm green. NOTE: the lane never filed this — it graded the run CLEAN ~1 minute into a 13.9-minute battery and moved on.

title: [P2] Harness reporting recurrences on this run: ci-pass is labelled 'act' when no workflow exists, ui-probe misses a Go-native dashboard, chaos-disconnect reads as HANGS on a 100s app suite, chaos-corruption false-green again
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 — cells recovered by hand-collecting the battery (QA-LANE-6)
review_notes: Recovered cells for trouble (agent ed361cdd, agent-host-2, 11 rows): (1) ci-pass detail begins 'act rc=1' although the repo has NO .github directory (`ls -d ~/trouble/.github` -> No such file), so the harness ran the native suite under an 'act' label — a misleading detail string that sends a reader hunting for a broken workflow; (2) ui-probe 'N/A — no web UI detected' while this repo ships a server-rendered dashboard (internal/dashboard, the v0.1 UI probe gap already recorded in the QA ledger note for trouble's 12:28Z row) -> repeat offence, the harness only detects node/web-framework UIs; (3) chaos-disconnect 'HANGS when network is cut (timeout 120s)' while the same cell's own output shows 'ok internal/app 100.799s' — the 120s window is shorter than the suite, exactly what QA-TROUBLE-2 diagnosed and downgraded; (4) chaos-corruption 'OK ... no Go files in <agent-home>/qa-trouble' = the QA-TROUBLE-3 false green repeating verbatim (harness BIN detection picks `go run .` for a cmd/ layout); it also truncated ./dagger.db, an untracked artifact, so the state-restart property stays UNVERIFIED. Fix direction: drop the hardcoded 'act' prefix (report the command actually run), teach ui-probe the Go-native http.Server pattern, size the chaos-disconnect window from the suite's observed duration, and gate chaos-corruption on a detected start command (UNVERIFIED when none).

acceptance_criteria: a .gitleaks.toml lands that (a) skips the gitignored .worktrees/ tree and (b) allowlists the deliberate test vectors/PEM fixtures by path+rule, with a one-line justification per allowlist entry
after the allowlist, `gitleaks dir .` reports 0 findings on main and the guard's secrets step PASSes on a diff that touches only examples/ + a test file
the guard's tests step no longer times out on this repo (either a bounded test_command / test_mode scoping, or an explicit documented exemption with the measured suite duration)
falsification: re-introduce one real-looking secret in a scratch commit and show the guard still catches it after the allowlist (the allowlist must not blind the gate)
a judge tier1 run on a fresh commit reports PASS/PASS on secrets+tests with no phantom failures
description: Measured on the TRBL-005 tick (2026-09-18, load_avg 16.45). (1) SECRETS: `gitleaks dir .` scans 451.9MB in 6m46s and reports 292 hits - generic-api-key 224, private-key 60, jwt 8. Split by tracked status: 255 hits are in gitignored .worktrees/** (legacy kanban worktrees that gitleaks does not skip: 20 per worktree from internal/scrub test vectors, 8 per worktree from specs) and 37 are in TRACKED files (internal/scrub/e2e_ledger_test.go 9, specs/SPEC-02-scrubbing.md 4, internal/scrub/ac_test.go 3, specs/SPEC-08-flow.md 3, internal/scrub/testdata/vectors/vectors.txt 2, internal/scrub/rules.go 2, internal/scrub/vectors_test.go 2, docs/specs-review.html 2, internal/dashboard/auth_test.go 1, internal/lifecycle/config_test.go 1) - all 32-char hex test vectors, PEM test fixtures and one JWT fixture, i.e. deliberate corpus data, not credentials. The repo ships no .gitleaks.toml, so 292 findings drown any REAL leak and every judge tier1 FAILs on every commit regardless of the diff (TRBL-001 shipped with the same artifact). (2) TESTS: the guard's tests step ends 'Command timed out' on test_command `go test ./... -count=1` - the suite is load-sensitive and takes 15-25 min under fleet load (per-package: app 106s, ledger 175s, dashboard 202s, sentinel 130s).
title: [P2] Guard tier1 is structurally red on this repo: the secrets step reports 292 gitleaks hits (255 inside the GITIGNORED .worktrees/, 37 tracked test vectors/spec examples, no .gitleaks.toml allowlist) and the tests step times out on `go test ./... -count=1`
reasoning: dogfood run 2026-09-17 — cell recovered by collecting the battery the QA lane closed CLEAN before it finished (QA-LANE-6)
review_notes: Evidence: TRBL-005 tick, .gitreins/history/2026-09-18/c2d5316a/verdict.json tier1 (secrets 292 leaks / tests 'Command timed out'), foreman gitleaks report and `go test ./... -count=1` log. Do NOT 'fix' this by deleting the fixtures - they are the scrub/sentinel corpus the specs require; the gate must learn which paths are data.

title: [P1] internal/sensors TestResolveManagers red on any host whose uid != 1000: dbus_test.go fixture hardcodes user:1000 so the self-vs-uid dedup never collapses (len 3, want 2)
reasoning: QA foreman cycle 2026-09-18 — fresh-system CI pass + chaos on agent-host-2 (agent 681b9e63, ci-pass cell)
review_notes: REPRODUCED on the clean QA agent in all three legs that run the suite (ci-pass act leg ci.log, ci-pass native leg native.log, chaos-resource 3G-cap leg res.log), identical line: internal/sensors TestResolveManagers — dbus_test.go:99 "managers = [system user:1018 user:1000], want system + one deduped uid". ROOT CAUSE read from source, not inferred: resolveManagers() (internal/sensors/dbus.go:478-510) dedupes correctly by uid (seen[uid] map), but the test fixture sets sensors.dbus.user_managers = ["self","user:1000","uid:1000","bogus"] and asserts len(got)==2 — which only holds when the TEST PROCESS uid is 1000, so "self" collides with user:1000/uid:1000 and the three real entries collapse to one. On the bunker agent (uid 1018) and under act (root = uid 0) "self" resolves to a DIFFERENT uid, two distinct uids survive dedup, len(got)==3, deterministic FAIL. The product code is correct; the assertion hardcodes the runner's uid, so `go test ./...` is red on every clean machine whose uid is not 1000 (any container running as root or a service user). REPRO (any non-1000 host): cd ~/trouble && go test ./internal/sensors/ -run TestResolveManagers -count=1 → "managers = [system user:<selfuid> user:1000], want system + one deduped uid". FIX SHAPE: build the fixture from os.Getuid() (fmt.Sprintf("user:%d", os.Getuid())) or use ["self","uid:<self>","bogus"] so the dedup path is exercised on every host. DEDUPE: distinct defect from the open rows on this board — TRBL-004 and QA-TROUBLE-1/2 cover the load-sensitive wall-clock/RSS budget family (TestAmortizedThroughput, TestDeriveNeverBlocks, TestRSSContributionIsBounded, TestScrubBudget); this failure is uid-dependent and load-independent (it also failed in the 3G-cap leg where sentinel/research/skills were green). Ambiguity stated honestly: it would pass on a single-user box running as uid 1000. Per-stage board rows (lint/tests/docker-build/compose-config) not applicable to this repo's deployed cell set; trouble has no .github (no CI workflow), so the 'act' label in the ci-pass detail is the harness-labeling defect already filed as QA-LANE-7, not a workflow break.
